prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in League City, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1181; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give you the details, but fine. [Name withheld for this test document.]
Q: Understood. Where were you when the collision occurred?
A: I was in the parking lot of a grocery store in League City, Texas. I had just pulled into a space near the cart return.
Q: Were you moving or parked at the time?
A: I was backing out of the space, going slowly, maybe five miles an hour.
Q: What happened next?
A: A car came down the lane from my right, and I didn't see it until it was almost on me. Their front bumper hit the rear driver's side of my vehicle.
Q: Did you hit your head or feel any injury at the time?
A: My head bounced off the window frame. I didn't think much of it at first, but within an hour I had a bad headache and felt dizzy.
Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care that evening. They said I have a concussion and told me to rest and avoid screens as much as I can.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. I get headaches most afternoons, I'm sensitive to bright light, and I've had trouble concentrating at work. I've been out for a few days.
Q: Did you lose consciousness at any point?
A: I don't think so. I remember everything from before and after the impact.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I was careful and the other driver was going too fast for the lane. I'd like my vehicle damage and medical bills covered.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Okay, thanks.
